questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Equation of a Tangent Line to a Curve at a Point
questions.problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=2{x}^{2}+x$ at the point $(1,3).$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{2}+x.$ Computing the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2}+x)=4x+1.\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute ${f}^{′}(1)$, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1)=4(1)+1=5\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=5$ and the coordinates of our point $(1,3),$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(3) & =5(x-1) \\ y & =5x-5+3 \\ y & =5x-2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=3{x}^{2}+4x$ at the point $(1,7).$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=3{x}^{2}+4x.$ Computing the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2}+4x)=6x+4.\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute ${f}^{′}(1)$, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1)=6(1)+4=10\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=10$ and the coordinates of our point $(1,7),$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(7) & =10(x-1) \\ y & =10x-10+7 \\ y & =10x-3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining where a Tangent Line Intersects an Axis
questions.problem: Find where the tangent to the curve $y=4{x}^{3}-9x-1$ at the point $(1,-6)$ intersects the $x$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=4{x}^{3}-9x-1.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{3}-9x-1)=12{x}^{2}-9\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
m={f}^{′}(-1)=12(1)^{2}-9=3.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-6) & =3(x-1) \\ y & =3x-3-6 \\ y & =3x-9.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $x$-axis, we set $y=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =3x-9 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $(3,0).$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining where a Tangent Line Intersects an Axis
questions.problem: Find where the tangent to the curve $y=2{x}^{5}-8x$ at the point $(1,-6)$ intersects the $y$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{5}-8x.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{5}-8x)=10{x}^{4}-8\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(1)=10(1)^{4}-8=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y+6 & =2(x-1) \\ y & =2x-2-6 \\ y & =2x-8.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $y$-axis, we set $x=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =2(0)-8 \\ y & =-8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $(0,-8).$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining where a Tangent Line Intersects an Axis
questions.problem: Find where the tangent to the curve $y=\frac{1}{x}+3$ at the point $(1,4)$ intersects the $y$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{1}{x}+3.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{x}+3)=-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
m={f}^{′}(1)=-\frac{1}{(1)^{2}}=-1.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-4 & =-(x-1) \\ y & =-x+1+4 \\ y & =5-x.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $y$-axis, we set $x=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =5-0 \\ y & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $(0,5).$
